title: The Salem witch trials

slides.text: 20 PEOPLE WERE EXECUTED AS WITCHES. THIS WAS THE JUDGE'S HOUSE.
Salem, Massachusetts. Early 1692. Two young girls begin having fits: screaming, twisting, crawling under furniture.
A doctor blamed witchcraft. The girls named three women. Then more names came.
Within months, more than 200 people were accused.
Nineteen were hanged at Proctor's Ledge. One man, Giles Corey, was pressed to death under heavy stones for refusing to enter a plea.
This house belonged to Judge Jonathan Corwin. It's the only building still standing with direct ties to the trials.
By 1693 it was over. Years later, a judge and 12 jurors publicly apologized.
In 1992, Salem dedicated this memorial: a stone bench for each person executed.
Every October, huge crowds come to Salem. The Witch House is open for tours.
